mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% within a 3-month window indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0, or Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction permits (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a contraction in consumer demand, leading to reduced corporate revenue expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 returns during the early stages of a recession.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is below 100, or Rank IC is below 0.01 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals strong economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% indicates rising inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0, or Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals a severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the interaction term is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals reduced consumer confidence in the housing market, leading to weaker overall demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and HOUST declines, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
